This is what I do for frozen custard. So easy we don't even need a web page.

1 cup milk, 6 eggs, 2/3 cup sugar, 1 cup heavy wipping cream, salt.

Whisk eggs, stir in milk and sugar.

Heat to 160F. The lazy way is to put a pan or dish in another pan full of water (glass dish allows you to be even lazier than a pan). Why is this lazy, because you can put the bottom pan at high heat without fearful monitoring. Just blast it with heat till you get the reading you want. Stir a bit as you heat. When the thermometer hits 150 turn off the heat. When it reaches 160 move the termomiter to the bigger pan and pour in tap water till it reads 160ish. Anywhere from 140-180 (just so long as it's not boiling really). Now stir it at that temperature for 10 minutes. This method requires abosolutely no second guessing yourself and doesn't wait for nature. (Or you can stand over a pot judging how high you can put the heat without scorching milkmaking constant adjustments like a sissy).

Some time during this stiring add coco and salt to taste. Just dust the top of the liquid and whisk it in to reduce the effort of mixing it considerably. Remember that you will be adding cream to this so rich is ok. It's hard to go wrong with either the coco or salt.

After that let it sit and cool on it's own till cool enough to refrigerate. Throw in the fridge over night covering it.

Now that you have the liquid custard made the easiest part comes in the morning. Simply add the cream, stir, and freeze. Tips: be sure to tip the stirring / freezing bowl on it's side and stir with a folding motion because the two really don't like to mix if you just do a plane circle because of difference in density. Rotate your angle of attack frequently and it should come together in 20 seconds insead of 5 minutes.

Press plastic wrap against the liquid and freeze.

Notes: 1. This is a high egg varient of a recipe I found. I do recommend the 6 eggs... or more. This gives you a custard you can't buy from a shop. More and more frozen desert shops are just becoming flavored frozen water shops. Frozen yogurt is just frozen water people. You are pay 6 dollars a pop for a slushy. 2. The next thing I might modify is reducing the amount of milk to reduce crystal size. I thought about writing it with less milk but I wasn't going to post a recipe that I haven't actually tried. Uping from 4 to 6 eggs was a good call this last batch though so my intuition is pretty good. Feel free to reduce the milk to 3/4 cup or 2/3 cup if really daring. You will get a creamier custard. The risk is accidentally forming an actual custard (solid). If that happens you can just eat that.

I may have added more tips than necissary. Heat eggs and milk, put in fridge, mix with cream, freeze. Everything else is just extra tips to make that easier. Zero thought heating method and a tip to stir the junk without wondering why it won't mix.

The #1 rule of making cooking easy is to not sweat it. I cannot and will not ever follow a recipee. If I use one I will disregard half of it. If you put edible ingredients together 1/20 it will be unedible. Everything else, you can't go wrong. Cooking is not a process where you absolutely must get every step right. Chefs will have you think that you must do it with their same skill or it will all fall apart. It's just not true. The extra techique they have is just from doing it over and over. Each can save some effort when and if you want to worry about it.

For example, adding tap water to the bottom pot to cool it.. completely unnecissary. If you miss that nothing bad will happen. But while you have a measuring cup with a pour spout out you might as well. Then you can forget the thermomiter entirely from that point on and you can heat that water all the way to boiling with out worry.
